qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: (1) Moat Barriers: High customer switching costs and razor-and-blade consumable lock-in. Nordson's precision dispensing equipment is custom-engineered directly into customer assembly lines and medical device specifications. While dispensing hardware represents <1% of total production line cost, dispenser failure causes catastrophic line shutdowns or product ruin. Customers rely on Nordson's proprietary replacement nozzles, valves, hoses, and tips (~45-50% recurring revenue). In medical, fluid components are locked into regulatory filings (FDA 510(k)/PMA). (2) Empirical Proof: 10-year median ROIC of 17.2%, gross margins consistently 53-56% across cycles, EBITDA margins of 30-32%, and 61 consecutive years of annual dividend increases. (3) Erosion Threats: Cyclical customer capex freezes in electronics/semiconductors; potential commoditization of lower-end fluid dispensing by Asian competitors; and integration execution on larger acquisitions (ARAG, Atrion).
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global precision dispensing and fluid management leader with embedded switching costs and 45-50% recurring aftermarket consumable revenue. Structurally insulated across all 5 macrotrends: active hardware enabler of automation (AI chip packaging, robotic assembly) and demographic healthcare tailwinds (medical fluid delivery), with zero unhedged exposure to energy or structural inflation. Balance sheet fortress with $660M+ FCF, 7.0x interest coverage, and LT debt/NI at 3.5x with rapid organic deleveraging. [5-10Y g: industrial/medical volume 3.0% + pricing power 1.5% + portfolio mix/reinvestment 1.5% - integration/cyclicality drag 0.5% + net share buybacks 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial performance anchors quality: 10-year median ROIC of 17.2%; gross margins exceptionally stable between 53% and 56% over 10+ years; EBITDA margins 30-32%. FY2025 revenue reached $2.79B with operating income of $711.7M and Net Income of $484.5M. Owner FCF was $661.1M in FY25 (136% conversion) and $491.8M in FY24 (105% conversion), exceeding the 80% FCF conversion threshold. Balance sheet is strong: Long-term debt reduced from $2.10B in FY24 to $1.68B in FY25 ($1.99B total debt) following the $800M Atrion acquisition; LT debt / Net Income is 3.47x (passes <= 4.0x); FY25 interest coverage (EBIT / Interest) is 7.04x ($711.7M / $101.1M, passes > 5.0x). Segment breakdown: Industrial Precision Solutions (~48%), Medical and Fluid Solutions (~28%), and Advanced Technology Solutions (~24%). 61 consecutive years of dividend growth.
